title: sprintf holds pointers into the format string across a to_s callback that String#replace frees
live_proof: upstream fixed it in 59552ecb8 (59552ecb8e0be2d4de78dc2d56eba2024260f639) (2026-04-10), which is in master and postdates the 4.0.0-rc2 pin (2026-03-12); the pin's tree has no such fix. Host ASan at the pin: heap-use-after-free (with MRB_HEAP_PAGE_SIZE=1: heap-use-after-free); the same case on master: no report
fidelity: the trigger is the Ruby test upstream added with its fix, extracted onto a self-contained harness that collects failures instead of aborting, so one script yields one verdict. It is upstream's own reproduction, not a reduction of ours; what it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it
fault_sites_why: host ASan at the pin (probe/native-control.sh NC_ASAN=1 build, MRBD_NO_BOXING, gcc -O1 -g), 2026-10-11 on p13: heap-use-after-free at sprintf.c:407, READ of size 1. That run uses no Capstone arm; it was taken after the virtual arms of 2026-10-11 had run and before the bounds-only and CheriBSD reruns of the same day.

sysalloc-none.oracle: completes and the harness reports PASS: the defect executes and is silent in every sense this arm can see

sysalloc-bounds.oracle: completes and the harness reports PASS: the defect executes and is silent in every sense this arm can see

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes and the harness reports PASS: the defect executes and nothing here sees it
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: completes, ["PASS"]; with the quarantine probe: 1238 frees, all 1238 quarantined, 0 allocations returned while quarantined, 0 sweeps -- the freed block was held, never reissued, so the stale pointer read the dead object and no other (2026-10-11, default revocation, revocation control faulting in the same boot)

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, mruby 4.0.0-rc2 as ported on musl mallocng (exact bounds, lifetime retirement on free); its GC object slots are unbounded offsets in a malloc'd heap page: a capability fault (cause 24-30) is CAUGHT, a run that completes is MISSED

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: the same with patch 0008 (MRBD_SUBLET=1): every GC object slot a CDERIVE child of its heap page, revoked by CREVOKE when the sweep frees it: as virtual-malloc

status: sysalloc-none and sysalloc-bounds measured 2026-10-06 on the Capstone application VM; cheribsd-revocation measured 2026-10-06 on CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation at its default; virtual-malloc and virtual-nested-pools measured 2026-10-11 on the virtual profile. The sublet-gc arm left the case with the Sublet heap and the GC-slot adapter on 2026-10-11; its readings stay in results/20261006.
